input: The book ties the movement of Uranus to the span of a basic human lifetime, about 84 years.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part I, Ch1 Science of Time

input: The author notes that many Vedic astrologers now add Uranus, Neptune and Pluto to their interpretation.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part I, Solar and Cosmic Astrology p.50

input: Uranus, Neptune and Pluto rank after the lunar nodes in importance, and only if one chooses to use them.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part II, Order of Planetary Significance p.68

input: Uranus is assigned the rajasic quality, Neptune the sattvic and Pluto the tamasic, with weak influence overall.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part II, Planets and Qualities of Nature pp.69-70

input: Uranus, Neptune and Pluto are usually overpowered by whichever planets they are associated with, as the lunar nodes are.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part II, Planets and Qualities of Nature pp.69-70

input: Uranus is mainly an airy planet, changeable and disruptive.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part II, Elements pp.71-72

input: Neptune is mainly watery and of a very subtle, almost etheric nature.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part II, Elements pp.71-72

input: Pluto is fiery with a secondary earth quality, similar to Mars.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part II, Elements pp.71-72

input: Uranus is cold, dry, light, sharp, fast, inventive, disturbing, isolating and destructive.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part II, Planetary Attributes pp.73-74

input: Neptune is cold, wet, light, subtle, cloudy, sensitive and diffusive.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part II, Planetary Attributes pp.73-74

input: Pluto is hot, dry, heavy, sharp, rough, aggressive, penetrating, isolating and disturbing.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part II, Planetary Attributes pp.73-74

input: Uranus signifies shock, disturbance, transformation, eccentricity and invention.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part II, Key Indicators pp.74-75

input: Neptune signifies psychic sensitivity, imagination, illusion and charm.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part II, Key Indicators pp.74-75

input: Pluto signifies will, domination, manipulation and catastrophes.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part II, Key Indicators pp.74-75

input: Uranus and Pluto are generally malefic, though less so than Rahu and Ketu, and Pluto seems the more malefic.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part II, Benefic or Malefic pp.77-78

input: Neptune is a weak mutable benefic, like Mercury but to a lesser degree.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part II, Benefic or Malefic pp.77-78

input: As distant planets, Uranus, Neptune and Pluto mostly magnify or transmit the influence of other planets, and are often strongest in transit.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part II, Benefic or Malefic pp.77-78

input: The author says most influences of the outer planets are already read through the lunar nodes, so they are not usually used and a reading can be done without them.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part II, Lunar Nodes: Uranus, Neptune and Pluto p.106

input: Pluto resembles Ketu and acts as the negative side of Mars, psychic and willful, leading to danger, suffering or even death.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part II, Lunar Nodes: Uranus, Neptune and Pluto p.106

input: Uranus relates to Saturn, is eccentric, erratic and strongly individualizing, can force spiritual change and may unbalance the mind if one is unaware of it.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part II, Lunar Nodes: Uranus, Neptune and Pluto p.106

input: Neptune relates to the secretive negative side of Jupiter, with a subtle Venus-like sensitizing and psychic effect over imagination, illusion, fantasy and charm.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part II, Lunar Nodes: Uranus, Neptune and Pluto p.106

input: Rahu is described as roughly Neptune and Uranus combined, joining Neptune's hallucinatory imagination with Uranus's shock.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part II, Lunar Nodes p.106

input: Vedic astrology does not accept Uranus, Neptune or Pluto as sign rulers, since giving them Aquarius, Pisces and Scorpio would break the orbital order of rulerships.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part II, The Signs pp.107-108

input: The author suggests indirect co-rulership: Pluto with the negative side of Mars, Neptune with the negative side of Jupiter, and Uranus with the positive side of Saturn.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part II, The Signs pp.107-108

input: Rahu and Ketu are often treated as co-rulers of Aquarius and Scorpio because they resemble Uranus and Pluto.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part II, The Signs pp.107-108

input: As a tentative suggestion, friendships and enmities of Uranus, Neptune and Pluto may be taken from Saturn, Jupiter and Mars respectively.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part II, Planetary Relationships p.128

input: Pluto appears, tentatively, to correspond most to the eighth house, death and the hidden will.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part III, House Significators pp.154-155

input: Neptune may be useful for the twelfth house, linked to imagination and the subconscious.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part III, House Significators pp.154-155

input: Uranus acts as a disrupting influence, like Saturn and the sixth house.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part III, House Significators pp.154-155

input: The author says the outer planets are outside the regular Vedic system, so no traditional aspect rules exist for them.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Ch4 Aspects for Uranus, Neptune and Pluto pp.174-175

input: The outer planets can be given the ordinary seventh-sign aspect, with conjunction treated as full interchange.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Ch4 Aspects for Uranus, Neptune and Pluto pp.174-175

input: For the outer planets the author often counts aspects by degree with an orb of about 10 degrees or less, since distant planets act more weakly.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Ch4 Aspects for Uranus, Neptune and Pluto pp.174-175

input: Optionally, special aspects may be given by resemblance: Uranus like Saturn (3rd and 10th), Neptune like Jupiter (5th and 9th), Pluto like Mars (4th and 8th).
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Ch4 Aspects for Uranus, Neptune and Pluto pp.174-175

input: Alternatively the outer planets may take the nodal special aspects of the 5th and 9th.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Ch4 Aspects for Uranus, Neptune and Pluto pp.174-175

input: The author is unsure outer planets should have special aspects, warning it would give them too much power and unbalance a chart unless treated as minor.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Ch4 Aspects for Uranus, Neptune and Pluto pp.174-175

input: Transits of Uranus, Neptune and Pluto, with Jupiter, Saturn and the nodes, are counted as distant-planet background for minor periods and often act for up to a year.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Ch5 Planetary Periods, Background Transits p.201

input: Uranus is classed as vata or air, a higher octave of Mercury.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Medical Astrology, Three Humors pp.215-216

input: Pluto is classed as pitta or fire, a higher octave of Mars.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Medical Astrology, Three Humors pp.215-216

input: Neptune is classed as kapha or water, a higher octave of Venus.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Medical Astrology, Three Humors pp.215-216

input: In Mozart's chart the Moon is closely conjunct Pluto in Scorpio, which the author takes to suggest possible poisoning, with death in the first year of the Moon major period.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part IV Chart 13 Mozart p.290

input: In Jim Jones's chart the Moon in Pisces in the fourth house is conjunct erratic Uranus, shown as an overly reactive mind.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part IV Chart 20 Jim Jones p.302

input: In Kubler-Ross's chart Pluto is counted among the chief malefic influences on a waning Moon near new.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part IV Chart 17 Kubler-Ross p.297

input: In the anorexia case chart Neptune sits at about 25 degrees Virgo in the first house, among five planets in the ascendant sign.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part IV Chart 29 Anorexia Case p.316

input: In the wife-murderer chart Pluto in Cancer in the seventh house is conjunct Mars and Saturn, and Mars's debility is reinforced by Saturn and manipulative Pluto rather than cancelled.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part IV Chart 30 Wife Murderer pp.317-318

input: The husband's Mars-Saturn-Pluto conjunction in Cancer falls in the wife's tenth house and aspects her ascendant, directing violence at it.
source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (modern author; tentative, outside classical Jyotish) | Part IV Chart 31 Murdered Wife p.320

input: The author states that Hindu astrology does not recognise any influence from the recently discovered planets Uranus, Neptune and Pluto, and works only with the seven classical planets plus the shadowy nodes Rahu and Kethu.
source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology (stance: classical Hindu astrology does not use them) | Chapter II, The Zodiac and the Solar System
